Cautiously supportive tone. Strong labor markets and moderate growth are offset by weak business fixed investment and exports and inflation below target. New Keynesian evidence (Galí and Gertler 1999; Woodford 2003; Christiano, Eichenbaum, and Evans 2005) highlights the role of expected inflation and the output gap, and with market-based inflation compensation low, easing is consistent with stabilizing inflation toward 2%. The rate cut and “ample reserves” operations via T-bill purchases and repos should support demand and monetary transmission; they can also ease financing frictions that weigh on capex and inventories, consistent with the interest rate–investment link and the internal-funds channel documented by Kashyap, Lamont, and Stein (1994). Empirical VAR evidence (Sims 1992) indicates monetary easing tends to lift real activity, aligning with the Committee’s outlook while acknowledging uncertainty. Overall, mildly positive but guarded.
